newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls on Belarus leaders to end dispute.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls on Belarus leaders to end dispute.

text.p: The United States on Thursday called on Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko to begin talks immediately with parliamentary leaders to resolve their dispute over a proposed constitution for the former Soviet republic.

The speaker of the Belarus parliament, Semyon Sharetsky, has accused Lukashenko of attempting to set up a dictatorship with a secretly drafted constitution that would dangerously increase the president's powers. The document is due to be put to national referendum Nov. 7.

"The proposed constitution under consideration would fail to provide any semblance of separation of powers, protection of individual freedom or rule of law," U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

Burns said the steps toward democracy taken by Belarus since independence were now in jeopardy, and called on Lukashenko "to enter immediately into consultations to find a compromise that protects basic human rights, the democratic process and fundamental freedoms, and avoids violence."
"Unfortunately, by declaring his unwillingness to work with parliament, President Lukashenko appears to be on a course that would further split the country," he said in a written statement.

The new constitution calls for a two-chamber parliament with a 110-seat majority-elected house of representatives and a regionally represented senate with a third of its members named by the president.
Lukashenko, 41, won presidential elections in 1994 on promises to restore order, fight corruption and repair the strong links with Russia that were disrupted by the collapse of the Soviet Union.
But during his period in office he has battled against nationalist opponents, trade unions and parliament.

Lukashenko signed a pact with Moscow in April to create a strong economic and political union which he believes could grow into a federation. But nationalist groups, scared by the prospect of renewed Moscow domination and Russia's backing for Lukashenko, protested the deal.
Lukashenko responded by cracking down on the nationalist opposition and jailing nearly 200 people for taking part in demonstrations against the pact.
The United States recently granted political asylum to two opposition leaders, Zenon Poznyak and Sergei Naumchik.
